intro: You're looking for a conveyancer who is both affordable and close to you, likely because you're buying, selling or remortgaging a home and want to keep the legal costs down. Price matters, but so does getting the job done properly. We can introduce you to a UK conveyancer who quotes you directly, so you can compare fees and make an informed choice.
need_heading: What people searching for a cheap conveyancer near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want a straightforward quote without hidden extras, from someone they can easily reach.
needs: You're buying your first home and need to know what the legal work will cost before you commit.
You're selling a property and want a conveyancer who charges a fair fee and keeps you updated.
You're remortgaging and need the legal side handled quickly and at a reasonable price.
You've had a quote that seemed low but worry it won't include searches, VAT or other disbursements.
You'd prefer a conveyancer you can visit or call locally if something needs sorting out face to face.
context: A low headline fee isn't always the cheapest overall. Ask what's included, such as searches, land registry fees and VAT, and whether there are extra charges for leasehold work or for dealing with a lender. A conveyancer who explains everything upfront can help you avoid surprises later.

Conveyancing is a reserved legal activity in England and Wales, carried out by solicitors regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority or by licensed conveyancers regulated by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers. Both must hold professional indemnity insurance and follow rules on handling client money, so you can check the firm's regulator before you instruct. Many lenders also require your conveyancer to be on their panel, so confirm that early.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say whether you're buying, selling or remortgaging, and whether it's a freehold or leasehold property.
Mention the approximate property value or price, as fees often depend on it.
Tell us if you have a mortgage offer and which lender you're using, so panel membership can be checked.
Explain if you're in a chain or have a tight deadline, as this can affect the service you need.
Let us know if you'd prefer a conveyancer you can visit in person or are happy to work remotely.
Include any specific concerns, such as a tight budget or a need for clear, fixed-fee pricing.
questions: What exactly does your quoted fee include, and what might be charged extra?
Are there additional costs for leasehold properties or for dealing with my lender?
Are you on my lender's panel, and if not, can you still act for me?
Which regulator are you regulated by, and what is your professional indemnity insurance cover?
How will you keep me updated on progress, and who will be my main point of contact?
Can you give me a full written quote with all disbursements and VAT shown separately?

faqs.q: Is the cheapest conveyancer always the best option?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. A low fee might not include searches, VAT or other costs, so ask for a full breakdown. Also consider whether the firm is on your lender's panel and how they communicate, as a slightly higher fee can save you stress later.

faqs.q: How can I check a conveyancer is properly regulated?
faqs.a: Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority, and licensed conveyancers by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers. You can check the firm's status with the relevant regulator. Both must hold professional indemnity insurance and follow rules on handling client money.

faqs.q: Do I need a conveyancer near me, or can I use one remotely?
faqs.a: Many conveyancing firms work remotely by phone, email and post, so distance isn't always a barrier. However, some people prefer a local firm they can visit if they need to sign documents or discuss things face to face. It's worth asking how they handle ID checks and original documents.

faqs.q: What should I do if my lender requires a conveyancer on their panel?
faqs.a: Tell the conveyancer your lender's name and ask if they are on that lender's panel. If not, you may need to choose a firm that is, or your lender might allow you to use your own conveyancer under certain conditions. Check with your lender before instructing.

extra_heading: Spotting a conveyancing quote that only looks cheap
extra: When a conveyancer advertises a very low fee, the figure is often for the basic freehold purchase only. Ask for the quote in writing and check whether searches, the land registry fee, VAT and bank transfer charges are included, because these are usually added on top and can change the final bill considerably.

Leasehold work is a common source of extra cost, as the conveyancer has to read the lease, obtain management information and deal with the freeholder or managing agent. If your property is leasehold, or if you are buying with a mortgage, ask specifically what those parts of the work will cost before you instruct anyone.

A local firm can be easier to reach if something needs sorting quickly, but many conveyancers work happily by phone, email and post. Weigh up the fee against how clearly the conveyancer explains the costs and how easily you can get hold of them, rather than choosing on price alone.

extra_faqs.q: Why do conveyancing quotes vary so much for the same property?
extra_faqs.a: Firms structure their fees differently and include different items, so one quote may exclude searches or VAT that another includes. Always ask for a full written quote with every disbursement listed, then compare like with like rather than the headline figure.

extra_faqs.q: Can I use a conveyancer who is not local to save money?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, distance is not usually a barrier, as most of the work is done by phone, email and post. What matters more is that the firm is on your lender's panel if you have a mortgage, and that you are comfortable with how they will keep you updated and handle original documents and ID checks.
